A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel approach for zero-shot learning of relation extraction, by reducing relation extraction to a reading comprehension task, which we can solve by leveraging recent neural reading comprehension techniques.

we propose a new paradigm for relation extraction, based on reading comprehension, which is more robust to the sparsity of training data and can generalize to new relation types without any labeled data.

we show that relation extraction, a task that has traditionally been treated as a classification problem, can be viewed as a reading-comprehension problem, and can benefit from the advances in the reading-comprehension community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
relation extraction is a reading comprehension task.

reading comprehension techniques can be used as a general-purpose tool for extracting information from unstructured text, and that the ability to ask questions about the text can be used to learn models that generalize beyond the questions that were used for training.

the reading-comprehension formulation of relation extraction is promising, and that the approach is likely to benefit from the recent explosion of interest in reading-comprehension tasks and techniques.
